British vocalist, musician, and artist. Born on 25 June 1945 in Hammersmith, London, England, UK. Brought up in London, Siffre is the son of an English mother and a Nigerian father. After jobs such as mini-cab driver and delivery man he started to concentrate on music full-time, leaving for Cannes, France to play guitar with a variety of soul musicians and bands. He returned to the UK in the late 1960s and enjoyed solo hits in 1971 with It Must Be Love (later covered by [a=Madness]) and Crying, Laughing, Loving, Lying. Although Watch Me (1972) was his last hit of the 1970s, he made a spectacular comeback with (Something Inside) So Strong (1987). In recent years Siffre's work has been reassessed by a new generation after the break from his song I Got The from the [m=171737] album (1975) was sampled by [a=Eminem] in his breakthrough hit [m=12114] (1999). Siffre nowadays spends much of his time writing poetry which deals with gay rights and other world issues.

The Dave Brubeck Quartet was a jazz quartet founded in 1951 by [a37737] on piano together with [a170329] on saxophone. The Dave Brubeck Quartet disbanded in 1967, and only met again for its 25th anniversary in 1976. The band name would later be used by the pianist for other groups that he led.

profile.profile:
Swedish multinational record label founded in 1949 by the brothers [a2393735] and [a=Anders Burman] together with their friend [a2785953] to release jazz. The name was taken from the American music magazine Metronome Magazine.

Label Code: LC 0270 / LC 00270.

In 1950, Mats Bjerke, together with [a=Bent Fabricius-Bjerre], opened an office in Denmark, [l=Metronome Records A/S]. In 1954 Bjerke and Fabricious-Bjerre expanded to West Germany, founding [l145463].

German Metronome also distributed many other labels in the 1970s, including the Ohr group of labels: [l=Ohr], [l=Die Kosmischen Kuriere] and [l=Kosmische Musik], and also took over distribution of the [l=MPS] label in late 1976 after BASF folded. In 1983 [l95013] had become part of the [l8742] group of companies which in turn became the German division of [l=Universal], with release duties handed over to [l312624]. German Metronome ceased oprations in late 1996.

Of the Scandinavian versions of Metronome, the Swedish [l121060] was sold to [l=WEA International Inc.] in 1979, later known as [l=Warner Music Sweden AB]. The Danish company seems to have had little output since the early 1980s and became Metronome Entertainment A/S in 1992.

See also [l297483] and [l373636].

Swedish releases often mention LC 4281 / LC 04281 due to the fact the Swedish Metronome company was acquired by [l1255] (now Warner Music) in 1979.
